  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The variable is continuous with reasonable range (0.5-201.4s), though right-skewed. Consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA if variance heterogeneity is severe. The large sample (n=76,655) provides power to detect small effects.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73. Standard ANOVA inappropriate due to binary nature and likely non-normal residuals. RECOMMENDATION: Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis as approximation. If ANOVA is insisted upon, interpret with extreme caution as effect size measure only.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Highly right-skewed (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47). Strongly consider log-transformation, winsorization, or robust methods. Check for extreme outliers that may drive variance.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Continuous variable with reasonable range. Check normality and homoscedasticity; transformation may not be needed.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38. Check for floor/ceiling effects and variance heterogeneity. Arcsine or logit transformation may improve normality if needed."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures within mice (8 mice, 9,500+ trials/mouse on average). Standard ANOVA assumes independence. RECOMMENDATION: Use mixed-effects model with Mouse as random intercept, or aggregate to mouse-level means for conservative analysis.",
    "Normality: Assess via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals. For large n, central limit theorem applies but skewed variables (Path Efficiency, Time-to-Target) may need transformation.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equal variances across paradigms. Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined: 48,846 vs Sham: 3,505) makes variance heterogeneity likely and problematic for standard ANOVA.",
    "Outliers: Examine boxplots and influence statistics. Path Efficiency shows extreme max value (29.8) suggesting outliers.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (63.7% of data). Weighted analyses or mixed models with REML recommended to handle unbalanced design."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant: Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Average Speed, AD), or Games-Howell if variances unequal.",
    "For Success (binary): Pairwise odds ratios from logistic regression with Bonferroni or FDR correction for 10 comparisons.",
    "For Path Efficiency: Robust post-hoc (Dunn's test) or bootstrap confidence intervals due to skewness.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs ICMS Only (visual contribution), Combined vs Dim Visual Only (ICMS contribution), both vs Sham (treatment effects), Bright vs Dim Visual (intensity effect).",
    "Correction for multiple testing: Bonferroni (conservative) or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across 5 response variables × 10 pairwise comparisons = 50 tests."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.27 vs 0.68-0.78), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lowest Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lowest AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40).",
    "Combined stimulation expected to show best or near-best performance: highest Success (0.78), lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.50), highest Average Speed (12.83), highest AD (0.40).",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only expected to perform intermediately and similarly to each other: Success ~0.68-0.69, Time-to-Target ~3.05-3.14s, Path Efficiency ~0.43, suggesting additive or synergistic effects of combined stimulation.",
    "Bright Visual Only may outperform Dim Visual Only: Success 0.78 vs 0.67, Time-to-Target 2.61s vs 3.14s, Path Efficiency 0.50 vs 0.43, suggesting visual intensity matters.",
    "AD pattern suggests stimulation increases angular dispersion (more exploratory/wider search pattern): Sham lowest (0.24), Combined highest (0.40), with visual-only and ICMS-only intermediate."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group imbalance: Combined paradigm has 14× more trials than Sham, 10× more than Bright Visual Only. Standard ANOVA assumes equal weighting; unweighted means may differ from observed means.",
    "Non-independence: Multiple trials per mouse violate independence assumption. Mouse-level clustering unaddressed in standard ANOVA.",
    "Binary Success variable: ANOVA theoretically inappropriate; logistic regression or generalized linear mixed model preferred.",
    "Skewed distributions: Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target show extreme right skew with outliers; mean comparisons may be misleading.",
    "No covariate adjustment: Learning effects across trials, trial order, or session effects not accounted for in simple paradigm comparison.",
    "Causal inference: Observational comparison of stimulation conditions without randomization within subjects; mouse-specific preferences may confound."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. Use restricted maximum likelihood (REML) for unbalanced data. For robustness, complement with mouse-level aggregation (n=8) using non-parametric methods, and report both individual-trial and mouse-level analyses to assess consistency. For Success specifically, use binomial GLMM with logit link. Consider Bayesian hierarchical modeling to properly quantify uncertainty given the complex data structure."
}
